US OFFICIALS ANNOUNCE ‘FIRST-EVER SEIZURE’ OF NORTH KOREAN SHIP ALLEGEDLY USED TO BUST SANCTIONS

https://cdn01.dailycaller.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/kim-jong-un-donald-trump-e1553283769313.jpg

17,061-ton ship that is registered in North Korea.

The Wise Honest was intercepted April 2, 2018, while carrying coal from North Korea. The ship had not operated its automatic signaling system since Aug. 4, 2017, according to the Justice Department.

The ship was used to “illicitly ship coal from North Korea and to deliver heavy machinery” to the North Korean government, the Justice Department said. Payments to maintain the vessel were reportedly made in American currency routed through unwitting American banks. (RELATED: North Korea Launches ‘Unidentified’ Rocket)

“This conduct violates longstanding U.S. law and United Nations Security Council resolutions,” reads a Justice Department press release.

https://cdn01.dailycaller.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/GettyImages-1128001817-620x413.jpg

(US President Donald Trump (R) walks with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un during a break in talks at the second US-North Korea summit at the Sofitel Legend Metropole hotel in Hanoi on February 28, 2019. (Photo by SAUL LOEB/AFP/Getty Images)

The seizure comes in the wake of escalating tensions between Washington and Pyongyang. North Korea has launched two short-range missiles in the past five days, even as President Donald Trump has claimed publicly that he hopes to continue negotiations over nuclear weapons with Kim Jong Un, North Korea’s dictator.

Trump made a surprise announcement March 22 on Twitter that he was withdrawing a new round of sanctions the Treasury Department had placed against North Korea earlier that day.

The Wise Honest was used by the Korea Songi Shipping Company to export coal from North Korea to foreign clients from November 2016 through April 2018. The ship in turn imported machinery to North Korea.

The company is an affiliate of the Korea Songi General Trading Corporation, which was sanctioned June 1, 2017, by the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control.

The Songi Trading Corporation is a subordinate of North Korea’s army, the government said.

As part of a scheme to mask the Wise Honest’s country of origin, the Songi company allegedly “falsely” listed other countries on shipping documents. A representative of Songi also allegedly routed over $750,000 in payments for coal shipments through unwitting U.S. banks.

Geoffrey Berman, the U.S. attorney for the southern district of New York, said the Wise Honest seizure was the “first-ever seizure” of a North Korean cargo ship alleged to have violated international sanctions.

“This scheme not only allowed North Korea to evade sanctions, but the Wise Honest was also used to import heavy machinery to North Korea, helping expand North Korea’s capabilities and continuing the cycle of sanctions evasion,” Berman said in a statement.

“With this seizure, we have significantly disrupted that cycle. We are willing and able to deploy the full array of law enforcement tools to detect, deter, and prosecute North Korea’s deceptive attempts to evade sanctions.”

Hard to provide specifics without knowing your field / education. Happy to provide more details if you wished to post your resume (leave off your name and names of any companies / schools / etc.)

In general:

  • Make sure you have a solid linkedin profile and it is up to date. I hate 'social media', but that's critical these days for the business world.
  • Page unless you have a graduate level degrees or numerous publications that can justify a second page.
  • Summary / Objective / Relevant experience. Key skill sets / key credentials if applicable.
  • If you are a family man, involved in church, etc. Add it! Employers can't ask these questions, but you can tip the decision balance by showing you are a well rounded person. "Volunteer Activities: Youth baseball coach. Youth Sunday school teacher. Food bank. Etc." This allows the interviewer to ask "Oh, I see you like baseball." Then you can tell them all about your family and what you do on the weekends. Most resume 'professionals' will tell you to stay away from personal stuff as you don't want to 'alienate' yourself against employers. But, I disagree. Most resumes are too sterile and I'm not allowed to ask personal questions. It's difficult to get to know a person without touching on their personal life a bit. I'm much happier with a candidate if I can get to know a bit about them outside of the job. (And .. whatever you are about ... it's better that they don't hire you because they find out something they don't like about you in the interview vs finding out later and everyone being miserable about it.)
  • Once you have an interview - make sure you do as much research as you can about the company / business before the interview. Also, used linked in to figure out more about your interviewer, etc. It shows interest / capability if you can ask good questions.

Good luck!

HR professional weighing in.

Contact information and name centered on top as a header. Draft a very, very strong one or two sentence objective/mission statement and label it one of those. State in the most succinct way possible your strengths and experience, and what you're trying to accomplish.

Most recent work experience next, to least recent. Tailor bullet point sentences beginning with an action word (look up overused resume action words, and use thesaurus.com to find different words if you don't know one), they should be one-liners that highlight something you did regularly or were responsible for in that job. ONLY your current job is a present tense action word, e.g.:

  • Tabulates and analyzes recruitment data to identify gaps and opportunities

And your past jobs should be in past tense, e.g.:

  • Conducted onboarding sessions for groups of new employees

After work experience, education.

After education, professional licenses.

After professional licenses, volunteerism.

In italics centered at the very bottom, 'References available upon request', or something similar. I've also seen a lot of 'References furnished upon request', and I enjoy the word furnished, but that's just me.

Include dates and highest title held in each company/firm, too. Month Year - Month Year is fine (October 2009 - June 2017).

Don't go crazy with graphics, use high quality resume paper, and have several folks review it for you, folks you know who will give honest and constructive feedback.

I'd be happy to review what you prepare, if you'd like. I went to school for this and it's my line of work.

Editing to add: don't get hung up trying to make it short. That's a rule of thumb for people coming out of school or in their first couple jobs. I've seen five page resumes way, way higher quality than single-pagers. At the same time I wouldn't use more than six strong action statements for each job.
